passage: Note from Kamal, Leela's father. Leela came to me on Sunday with a plan: teach maths to two younger children in our building for 50 rupees a session, twice a week. She asked me first whether it was allowed, and asked me to speak to their parents, which I did. The lessons happen at our dining table, with me in the next room. She prepares worksheets on Sunday night, which I never asked for. Half of what she earns goes into the tin for her secondhand bicycle. She showed me the sums: her target date has moved from December to October, and she is pleased but tired on Wednesdays. I have told her that school work comes first, and we will review it in a month.

qa.q: How much does Leela charge for each session?
What is Leela feeling about the extra work, and how can you tell?
qa.a: She is pleased but a little tired, since she proudly shows the sums with the date moved earlier, yet she is tired on Wednesdays.

qa.q: What could Leela do if the tutoring gets too tiring?
qa.a: She could cut to one session a week or trim some spending, since the goal should not cost her school work.

qa.q: How might the children's parents see the tutoring?
qa.a: They may feel glad to have a trusted older neighbour helping their children for a small fee, especially since Kamal spoke to them first.

grounding: A student offers small honest tutoring after checking with parents and puts part of the earnings toward the same goal, speeding it up.

passage:
Tuesday
First proper week as a tutor! Before I offered, I asked Mummy and Papa. Papa said yes if it's only in our building, only before seven in the evening, and in the child's home with a parent around. Mummy said to keep it small so my own studies don't slip.
So now it's Abhinav from 3B (Class Four) and his friend from the fourth floor, maths and English, Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 5 to 6. Their mothers pay a small fee at the end of each month; we agreed the amount together, with Mummy there.
Abhinav got 9 out of 10 on his tables test today and did a little dance.
Plan for the money: half into my laptop jar, which I've been filling from pocket money since January, and the rest is mine. With the tutoring, the jar should fill by Diwali instead of next summer.
– Ritu

qa.q: How did Ritu feel when Abhinav got 9 out of 10?
qa.a: Ritu felt proud and happy, delighted by the little dance.

qa.q: What else could Ritu keep in mind as the tutoring continues?
qa.a: Checking with Mummy every few weeks that her own studies aren't slipping, and cutting hours if they are.

qa.q: How might Abhinav's mother see the arrangement?
qa.a: She likely values affordable, safe help at home, with the fee agreed openly and a parent present.

grounding: Shows a student tutoring younger neighbours for a small fee after checking with parents, and putting part of the earnings toward a saving goal.
